originality.rationale: The structural four-phase classification for counting-free two-variable logic in the loop-retaining one-sorted polarity signature is not established by the inspected orthogonal-polarity graph papers or by the accessible earlier incidence-geometry and graph-logical claims. The result is not a mere rephrasing of the geometric oval/absolute-line dichotomy: sharp exceptions arise from positive versus zero counts of distinct nonneighbors in the internally defined types, and a permanent two-pebble strategy is needed for unrestricted depth. Searches and implication comparisons reveal no dominating theorem; unresolved priority risks are acknowledged.

value.rationale: An exact all-plane logical classification, with four nonempty phases, canonical smallest-order exemplars 2,4,3,5, and sharp one-versus-two variable boundary, is a motivated new structural invariant of orthogonal-polarity adjacency. Two small-order obstructions have precise mathematical sources in missing within-type nonneighbors. The claim is not a routine finite enumeration and applies independently of any coordinatization.
